elements.quote: Worldwide, surgery related deaths within 30 days of the procedure accounts the third contributor among all causes of deaths, with an estimated 4.2 million people annually and half of these deaths occur in low and middle income countries.
elements.reason: The Introduction provides some context on the burden of surgery-related deaths, but the retrieved evidence does not show a description of the current state of knowledge on SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia or explicit uncertainties/knowledge gaps.
The retrieved evidence does not contain an explicit explanation of the importance of or need for conducting this review in the context of existing knowledge.

No retrieved evidence identifies or cites any previous systematic review on this topic or explains the need for an update/replication; the PROSPERO check (text_10) addresses duplication of registrations, not justification relative to prior published reviews.
This is a review of prevalence and predictors of SSI after cesarean section, not a review of intervention effects, so no mechanism of action needs to be described.
The review addresses prevalence and predictors of an outcome, not a complex intervention or delivery context, so a logic model is not required.

elements.quote: To determine the pooled prevalence of SSI following cesarean section and its predictors in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: An explicit Objective section states the review objective clearly, covering both prevalence and predictors.
This is a review of prevalence and associated factors (etiology/predictors), not an intervention-effect review, so PICO-planned comparisons do not apply.

elements.quote: This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. elements.reason: Eligibility criteria specify setting (all regions of Ethiopia), outcome (prevalence/incidence of SSI and/or associated factors), and eligible study designs (observational: case-control, cross-sectional, cohort).
